article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-Dominant Hybrid
Genetics: Tina × Grease Monkey
Breeder: Exotic Genetix
THC Content: 22–25%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , Limonene , Myrcene
Primary Flavors: Roasted Coffee, Dark Chocolate, Diesel
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 Weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: September / October
Indoor Yield: Heavy
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Coffee, chocolate, and gasoline might sound like an unlikely combination, but Slippery Susan brings these contrasting aromas together with remarkable intensity. Developed by Exotic Genetix, this indica-dominant cannabis hybrid combines the award-winning Tina with the exceptionally resinous Grease Monkey, producing marijuana flowers with a distinctive dark, frosted appearance. Beneath their shimmering trichomes lies an aromatic profile resembling freshly roasted coffee beans, cocoa, earthy diesel, and sweet cookie dough.

The cultivar’s unusual fragrance is matched by its substantial potency and reputation for pronounced physical relaxation. Although the experience may begin with a pleasant cerebral uplift, its heavier effects can eventually become deeply calming and sedating. With its recognizable OG ancestry, impressive resin production, and relatively short flowering period, Slippery Susan offers a compelling alternative to the fruit-candy genetics frequently associated with contemporary weed.
Genetics and Lineage

Slippery Susan originated within the Exotic Genetix breeding program through a cross between Tina and Grease Monkey. Tina provides an especially influential genetic foundation, having been created by combining Constantine with Triple OG. Constantine itself descends from Orange Valley OG and The Cube, connecting its background to established OG Kush and citrus-oriented cannabis genetics. Triple OG incorporates influences from Triangle Kush , Constantine, and Master Yoda, introducing additional earthy fuel, spice, and physically relaxing characteristics. Tina gained recognition after winning first place for Best Indica Flower at the 2017 High Times Southern California Harvest Cup. Its pungent jet-fuel fragrance, powerful effects, and substantial flower production made it particularly valuable for subsequent breeding projects.

Grease Monkey contributes the second half of the pedigree, introducing one of Exotic Genetix’s most recognizable resin-producing genetic lines. Created from GG4 and Cookies & Cream , this parent combines the aggressive diesel characteristics of classic glue genetics with a softer dessert-oriented aromatic profile. GG4, originally known as Gorilla Glue #4 , traces its ancestry to Chem’s Sister, Sour Dubb, and Chocolate Diesel , providing a background associated with sticky flowers and penetrating fuel aromas. Cookies & Cream descends from Starfighter and a Girl Scout Cookies selection, adding creamy vanilla, sweet dough, and earthy complexity. Together, these influences help explain the roasted-coffee, chocolate, and diesel characteristics associated with the finished hybrid.

The combination is generally classified as indica-dominant, although published indica-to-sativa percentages vary considerably. Its genetic identity is better understood through its parentage than through a fixed numerical ratio. Phenotypic differences can also influence flower density, coloration, aroma, and perceived effects. Certain plants may emphasize Tina’s sharp OG fuel character, while others develop greater sweetness and heavier cookie aromas from Grease Monkey. This variation offers cultivators opportunities to identify selections with particularly desirable resin production, aromatic complexity, and flowering characteristics.
Effects and Experience

The experience associated with Slippery Susan can begin with an unexpectedly noticeable cerebral sensation. Shortly after inhalation, some consumers describe a feeling of mental warmth accompanied by mild euphoria and increased enjoyment of their surroundings. Conversation, music, and familiar entertainment may become more engaging during this opening phase. Unlike intensely stimulating sativa-oriented varieties, however, the mental uplift is generally described as comfortable rather than energetic. A slightly dreamy quality can develop as the psychoactive effects intensify, making ordinary thoughts feel more immersive while gradually reducing the desire for demanding activities.

Physical relaxation becomes increasingly prominent as the experience progresses. A spreading sensation of heaviness may encourage sitting or reclining, while muscular tension can feel less noticeable. The initial mental stimulation often gives way to a considerably calmer state, occasionally accompanied by substantial appetite stimulation. With larger servings, the experience may develop into pronounced couch-lock, making movement feel less appealing and concentration more difficult. Sleepiness is another commonly described characteristic, particularly during the later stages. These qualities make the cultivar more closely associated with relaxed evening recreation than activities requiring sustained alertness.

Potency is an important consideration because commercially tested Slippery Susan flower has reached THC concentrations above 22%, with some seed descriptions advertising considerably higher potential. Actual cannabinoid content depends on phenotype, cultivation conditions, and individual harvests. Consumers with limited THC tolerance may find its relaxing effects unusually intense. Excessive consumption can produce dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, anxiety, increased heart rate, and temporary impairment of memory or coordination. Even experienced consumers should evaluate unfamiliar batches cautiously, since the combination of substantial THC exposure and delayed physical heaviness can make the experience stronger than initially anticipated.
Medical Benefits

Slippery Susan may attract medical marijuana patients interested in cannabis products associated with pronounced physical relaxation, appetite stimulation, and nighttime comfort. Its reported effects could appeal to individuals experiencing persistent discomfort or difficulty unwinding after demanding activities. Research involving THC-containing cannabis has identified modest benefits for certain chronic pain conditions, particularly some forms of neuropathic pain. However, clinical findings involving standardized cannabinoid preparations cannot automatically be applied to individual marijuana strains. No controlled clinical trials have established Slippery Susan itself as an effective treatment for chronic pain, inflammation, or another specific medical disorder.

Sleep-related symptoms represent another area of potential interest because the cultivar is frequently described as producing substantial sleepiness after its initial euphoric phase. Some individuals find THC-containing products temporarily helpful for perceived sleep onset, although research on long-term sleep quality remains inconsistent. Frequent consumption can contribute to tolerance, dependence, and sleep disturbances, while higher THC doses may worsen anxiety or produce uncomfortable psychological reactions. Appetite stimulation is also possible, but it should not be interpreted as evidence of effectiveness for treating a specific appetite disorder. Patients considering high-potency cannabis should discuss medication interactions, individual health risks, and appropriate treatment options with a qualified healthcare professional.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The fragrance of Slippery Susan occupies an unusual space between traditional OG pungency and rich dessert-oriented cannabis. Opening a container of properly cured flower can release a concentrated aroma resembling freshly roasted coffee beans, dark chocolate, and earthy diesel. A deeper background of damp soil, woody spice, and skunky gas reinforces the influence of its Tina ancestry. Meanwhile, Grease Monkey contributes a softer sweetness reminiscent of vanilla cookies and toasted pastry. The combination creates an aromatic profile that feels warmer and heavier than the bright fruit fragrances associated with many contemporary hybrids. Breaking apart the buds can intensify the diesel character while revealing additional cocoa-like richness.

Its flavor can present several distinct stages. An initial impression of earthy coffee and mild bitterness may transition into smoother chocolate, creamy dough, and subtle sweetness. As the smoke or vapor develops, pungent fuel and peppery spice become more apparent, creating a heavier finish that can linger on the palate. Some phenotypes emphasize dark roasted flavors, while others display greater cookie sweetness or sharp gasoline undertones. The resulting profile is especially appealing to consumers who appreciate traditional kush flavors but want something more complex than straightforward pine, earth, or diesel. Proper curing helps preserve the softer chocolate and cream characteristics without allowing the aggressive fuel aromas to overwhelm them completely.

Beta-caryophyllene and limonene have appeared among the most prominent terpenes in commercially tested Slippery Susan flower, with myrcene and humulene also contributing to its aromatic complexity. One tested batch contained approximately 0.47% beta-caryophyllene, 0.46% limonene, and 0.22% myrcene, illustrating how different compounds can occur at meaningful concentrations within the same harvest. Caryophyllene contributes peppery and woody qualities, limonene offers citrus-like brightness, myrcene introduces earthy and herbal characteristics, and humulene provides additional woody depth. However, the recognizable coffee and chocolate fragrances cannot be attributed to individual terpenes alone. Additional volatile aromatic compounds influence the finished profile, and concentrations vary between harvests.
Growing Information

Slippery Susan develops into a medium-to-tall cannabis plant with vigorous branching and a structure capable of supporting substantial flower production. Exotic Genetix describes the cultivar as suitable for both sea-of-green arrangements and multi-topped bush cultivation, reflecting its adaptability to different growing environments. Mature plants commonly display deep green foliage beneath resin-heavy flowers that can appear almost silver because of their dense trichome coverage. Dark red or rust-colored pistils create a striking contrast against the frosted bud surfaces. Certain phenotypes may also develop purple undertones inherited through Tina’s genetic background. Its compact, resinous flowers frequently carry a strong fragrance even before reaching full maturity.

Indoor flowering generally requires 56–63 days, placing this weed strain within the eight-to-nine-week category. Its medium-to-tall structure makes early canopy management beneficial, particularly when developing several productive branches rather than relying exclusively on one central cola. Topping and low-stress training can help maintain an even canopy, while appropriate spacing supports light penetration and air circulation. The flowers can become exceptionally dense as flowering progresses, making humidity management particularly important during the final weeks. Excessive moisture trapped inside compact buds increases the risk of mold and other fungal problems. The breeder characterizes its yield potential as heavy, although standardized production figures expressed in grams per square meter have not been consistently established.

Outdoor cultivation is possible in suitable climates, especially where plants receive abundant sunlight and adequate airflow throughout flowering. Its growth structure can support substantial branching when sufficient space is available, although heavy flowers may require additional support as they mature. Harvest generally occurs during autumn in favorable Northern Hemisphere environments, with precise timing determined by latitude, weather, and individual phenotype. The cultivar’s strong diesel-coffee fragrance can become particularly noticeable during late flowering, making odor management an important consideration for enclosed cultivation facilities. Following harvest, controlled drying and careful curing are essential for retaining the delicate chocolate and cookie notes alongside its heavier gas characteristics. Intermediate growers are generally best equipped to manage its vigorous development, dense flowers, and environmental requirements.
FAQ
Is Slippery Susan an indica or sativa strain?

Slippery Susan is an indica-dominant hybrid developed by Exotic Genetix. Published classifications vary regarding its exact indica-to-sativa ratio, but the cultivar is generally associated with pronounced physical relaxation and potentially sedating effects. Its experience may begin with cerebral euphoria before progressing into substantial bodily heaviness.
What are the genetics of Slippery Susan?

Exotic Genetix created Slippery Susan by crossing Tina with Grease Monkey. Tina originates from Constantine and Triple OG, while Grease Monkey combines GG4 with Cookies & Cream. This lineage introduces powerful OG genetics, sticky resin production, roasted-coffee aromas, chocolate undertones, and pungent diesel characteristics.
How strong is Slippery Susan weed?

Commercially tested Slippery Susan flower has contained THC concentrations around 22–25%, while certain seed descriptions advertise higher potency potential. Actual cannabinoid levels vary between harvests and individual phenotypes. Its reputation for pronounced physical relaxation makes it particularly important for inexperienced consumers to approach the strain cautiously.
What does Slippery Susan taste and smell like?

The dominant aromatic characteristics include roasted coffee, dark chocolate, earthy diesel, sweet cookies, and woody spice. Some phenotypes develop stronger vanilla or creamy undertones, while others emphasize pungent gasoline and skunky earthiness. Its coffee-and-chocolate fragrance distinguishes it from conventional fruity or candy-oriented cannabis hybrids.
How long does Slippery Susan take to flower?

Indoor flowering generally requires approximately 56–63 days, or eight to nine weeks. Exotic Genetix describes the plant as medium-to-tall, suitable for sea-of-green and multi-topped bush cultivation, and capable of heavy yields. Outdoor finishing dates depend on local climate, seasonal conditions, and individual plant maturity.
Final Thoughts on Slippery Susan

Slippery Susan brings together two important branches of Exotic Genetix’s breeding history, combining Tina’s award-winning OG characteristics with the resin-producing strength of Grease Monkey. The resulting cultivar offers a notably different aromatic experience from the sweet tropical and candy-flavored hybrids dominating many modern cannabis collections. Roasted coffee, chocolate, earthy diesel, and creamy cookies create a layered fragrance, while its silver-frosted flowers and dark pistils contribute considerable visual appeal.

For experienced marijuana consumers, the cultivar’s strongest attraction lies in its substantial potency potential and progression toward deep physical relaxation. Growers may appreciate its relatively short flowering period, productive branching, heavy yield potential, and exceptionally resinous buds. Although individual phenotypes vary, Slippery Susan remains a distinctive example of contemporary OG-and-Cookies breeding, offering a rich, roasted flavor profile and a powerful indica-dominant character that sets it apart from more conventional dessert hybrids .
